There is a right breaking off the northern groyne, as well as a left to the south. The waves are hollow and heavy. The swell angle is important as the rivermouth can cut out some of the size.

surfMetadata.guideSummary: Consolação is the fortress-adorned headland at the southern end of Supertubos beach. It delivers nice, heavy waves on both sides: a reefy, although somewhat fat, right-hand pointbreak, and a heavy, more stacked up sand-bottomed left. The right is a local favorite when the swell wraps around the headland and can hold size up to triple overhead. The left needs bigger swells to come to life and is a more volatile and dependable on sand placement on the bottom.

Since then, Nazaré has become a household name, one of Portugal's main coastal tourist attractions, a (former) stop on the Big Wave World Tour, and ground zero for big wave tow surfing. On the days when the offshore canyon isn't focusing huge swells into 80-foot peaks, Nazaré's inside sand bar produces heavy, hollow tubes in sizes that mortals can appreciate (as long as those mortals are barrel-riding experts).
